documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Outside vascular surgery group. Consult 01/13/2026. Sent 03/03/2026 after second request.

Reason: symptomatic right ICA stenosis.
History: 70-year-old man with a single 10-minute episode of right monocular vision loss on 12/1/2025, none since. Duplex at that visit: right ICA 50-69%, left without significant stenosis. HFpEF with admission 8/2025; lung adenocarcinoma treated with SBRT 2024; low-grade bladder cancer resected 2023. Former smoker, quit 2012.
Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, metoprolol 50 BID, HCTZ 25, furosemide 40; clopidogrel course completed. NKDA.
Exam: alert, neurologically intact. No cervical bruit.
Assessment: symptomatic moderate right ICA stenosis.
Discussion: reviewed endarterectomy versus best medical therapy. Considering his heart failure, treated lung cancer and age, we and the patient chose medical management: aspirin, statin, blood pressure control.
Plan: repeat carotid duplex in 6 months; return sooner for any new symptoms.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt says he saw vascular surgery on the 13th and they decided 'no surgery for now.' Requested the consult note from their office.

documents.title: Vascular letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vascular note from January (requested twice). Medical management of R ICA 50-69%, repeat duplex July. No changes to his list.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast, 18 months after SBRT. Comparison 9/16/2025. Right upper lobe post-radiation fibrosis unchanged. No new pulmonary nodules. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Stable treatment-related fibrosis. No evidence of recurrence.

documents.title: 18-month CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rad onc surveillance CT: stable, no recurrence. Next in 6 months per their schedule.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check. Roomed 35 min late - the clinic was running behind after an add-on.
Usually easygoing and on time. Today short with the MA at intake, called the wait room 'a disaster.' When I came in he cut me off: said he's tired of waiting every single time and won't be treated like he doesn't matter. Arms crossed, not looking at me.
I acknowledged the wait was long and that his time matters, and apologized. Asked if anything else was going on - says no, just fed up. Settled after a few minutes and we went on.
Interval: no further vision episodes. No dyspnea beyond baseline, weights steady ~154. Legs fine on atorvastatin. No hematuria.
PHQ-2 1. Denies feeling down most days.
Exam: lungs clear, RRR, no edema. Neuro nonfocal.
A/P:
1. Situational irritability over the wait - addressed; no mood disorder suspected. Will check in next visit.
2. HTN/HFpEF - stable, continue all.
3. R ICA stenosis, medical management - repeat duplex July per vascular.
4. Lung adenoca s/p SBRT, bladder ca s/p TURBT - surveillance per specialists, both clear.
5. Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.
Front desk asked to book him first slot of the day next time. RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Talbot, your labs from yesterday are stable - kidneys, potassium, blood count all normal and cholesterol where it has been. No changes. Your July visit is booked for 8:00 am, first appointment of the day.

documents.title: Appointment reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Reminder call for 7/31 8:00 visit. Pt confirmed, also has the vascular ultrasound on 7/14. No concerns.

reports.text: Bilateral carotid duplex, 6-month follow-up. Comparison 12/1/2025. Right ICA: plaque at origin, velocities in the 50-69% range, unchanged. Left ICA: no hemodynamically significant stenosis. Vertebral arteries antegrade.

documents.title: Carotid duplex
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vascular's repeat duplex report received: R ICA 50-69% unchanged. Continue medical management.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First slot, roomed on time. He opened by apologizing for May - 'I was a bear that day.' No hard feelings; irritability resolved.
Feels well. Walking most mornings. Weights 153-155. No orthopnea, no swelling. No vision changes.
Carotid duplex 7/14 stable.
Exam: lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.
A/P: HTN/HFpEF stable - continue lisinopril, metoprolol, HCTZ, furosemide. Atorva 40 and ASA. BMP today. Urology scope in August, rad onc CT in September. RTC 3 months with flu shot.

documents.title: Lab result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your kidney function and potassium from Friday are normal. Keep everything the same.

documents.title: Surveillance cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Office cystoscopy 08/11/2026. Hx low-grade pTa urothelial carcinoma, TURBT 8/2023, three clear scopes since. Today: normal urethra, bladder mucosa without papillary or flat lesions, healed right lateral wall scar. No recurrence. Continue yearly cystoscopy.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request: metoprolol tartrate 50 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, 90 days. Seen 7/31, BMP normal. Approved, 1 refill each until next visit.
